domain_label: Turlock & Central Valley Food & Dining Supply Chain and Sourcing
purpose: A session-bounded method for an independent Turlock food operator to design, set up, and harden a sourcing system across broadline distributors, cash-and-carry, local Central Valley ag (dairy, produce, meat), tortilla/masa and carniceria supply, specialty ethnic importers (Mexican, Assyrian/Middle-Eastern, Portuguese/Azorean), coffee roasters, equipment and smallwares, and waste/grease haulers, by mapping the cost center per format, choosing the right channel mix, exploiting the genuine Valley input advantage, protecting cold chain and food safety, and building resilience against price swings and supplier consolidation.
assumptions: no per-operator purchasing dataset is supplied; channel mixes and cost-share weights are reasoned heuristic priors keyed to the food_dining deep-dive, not invoices

the operator runs one of the 40 independent Turlock formats profiled in the deep-dive (taqueria, panaderia, mariscos, cafe, bakery, Italian/pizzeria, Assyrian, fine dining, ice cream, gastropub, truck)
the geography is Turlock / Stanislaus County in the Modesto MSA, ~15 miles from Sysco Central California, inside California's top dairy and produce belt, in 2026

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference, not confirmed contracts, unless the deep-dive cites the relationship (only La Mo's local-farm sourcing and Ishtar's own market are structurally documented)

per-business dollar revenue is never asserted; any dollar figure is a labeled benchmark estimate (food-cost share x format band) tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path
the operator holds or is obtaining the required county food-facility health permit and, for trucks, a commissary
exclusions: per-business revenue, profit, or sales-tax actuals stated as fact (only labeled benchmark estimates and cited public fee/benchmark figures are used)
menu engineering, recipe design, and front-of-house service (covered by other sector KBs)
site selection, lease negotiation, and the buildout/capex financing decision beyond the equipment-and-smallwares sourcing node
marketing, demand forecasting, and saturation/white-space strategy (covered by the market-saturation KB)
labor hiring, wage bands, and staffing models (covered by the Turlock wage-jobs KB)
alcohol licensing strategy beyond naming the beverage-wholesaler supply node and the Type 41/47 fee facts
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for Turlock/Central Valley food-and-dining supply-chain work units, grounded in the food_dining sector deep-dive (DEEPDIVE.md, reconciled.md, businesses.json, count=40): its named supplier universe (Sysco Central California Modesto, US Foods, Restaurant Depot, tortilla/masa houses, Mediterranean/Assyrian importers, seafood wholesalers, regional roasters), its per-format input cost centers, its published cost-structure benchmarks, and its permit/commissary/license fee facts; no supplied purchasing dataset
source_citation: Turlock Food & Dining Sector Deep-Dive (FACTORY/turlock_business/analysis/food_dining/DEEPDIVE.md sec 3-4, reconciled.md, businesses.json); Sysco Central California (Modesto) and US Foods locations; Restaurant Depot membership cash-and-carry; tortilla/masa suppliers (The Tortilla Plug, Romero's Food Products, Mi Rancho, Masienda, local Tortilleria Tres Hermanos); Mediterranean/Assyrian importers (Sadaf/Soofer, Zarrin, Karabetian, Macar) and local Assyrian grocers (Nineveh Imports, International Bazar, Neesan Market); seafood wholesalers (Pucci Foods, Santa Monica Seafood, Sierra Gold, Catalina Offshore); regional roaster (Chatz Roasting, Ceres); Stanislaus County Environmental Health food program and mobile-food commissary rule; City of Turlock mobile-vendor ($900) and business-license ($114) fees; CA ABC Type 41/47 fee schedule; BLS/industry cost-structure benchmarks cited in the deep-dive; heuristic priors where no purchasing dataset is supplied

competency_questions.question: For this specific Turlock format, what is the dominant input cost center, and which inputs must the sourcing plan protect first?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_COST_PROFILE names the format's bold cost center from the deep-dive (e.g., marinated meats for taqueria, fresh seafood for mariscos, mozzarella for pizzeria, hand-shaping labor plus flour for panaderia, roasted coffee for cafe) and ranks inputs by cost share and risk

competency_questions.question: What is the realistic supplier universe verified to serve Turlock/Modesto/Central Valley, and how is it segmented by channel?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPLIER_UNIVERSE enumerates the broadline, cash-and-carry, local-ag, tortilla/masa, ethnic-importer, seafood, roaster, equipment, and waste nodes named in the deep-dive and tags each as verified-to-serve vs representative inference

competency_questions.question: How should the operator split spend across broadline, cash-and-carry, and local/direct channels, and what drives the mix?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_MIX produces a reasoned percentage split across broadline, cash-and-carry, and local/direct keyed to volume, format, and the cost-vs-resilience tradeoff, not a single-source default

competency_questions.question: When does a broadline distributor like Sysco Modesto beat cash-and-carry like Restaurant Depot, and vice versa?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BROADLINE_RELATIONSHIP and CASH_AND_CARRY contrast delivery/credit/minimums/one-stop against membership/pay-now/no-delivery/lower-unit-cost and give a volume threshold rule

competency_questions.question: How does an operator capture the genuine Central Valley local-input advantage on dairy, produce, eggs, and meat?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOCAL_AG_DIRECT explains the short-freight, direct-from-grower/carniceria/dairy edge the deep-dive documents and which formats (creamery, pizzeria, cafe, panaderia, fine dining) benefit most

competency_questions.question: How is tortilla/masa and carniceria supply set up for taqueria, truck, and sit-down Mexican formats?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MASA_TORTILLA_CARNICERIA names the tortilla/masa houses and local tortilleria/carniceria options, distinguishes heirloom-masa from commodity, and matches lot size to truck-vs-restaurant volume

competency_questions.question: How does an operator source specialty ethnic inputs the broadline does not carry (Assyrian/Middle-Eastern, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican specialty, Asian)?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ETHNIC_IMPORTERS maps each community's importer and local-grocer supply (Sadaf/Zarrin/Karabetian/Macar and Nineveh/International Bazar/Neesan for Assyrian; Portuguese/Azorean specialty; Bay Area Asian importers) and notes which local markets double as supply

competency_questions.question: How is fresh seafood sourced and its cold chain protected for the mariscos format, the highest food-cost and highest-risk case?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SEAFOOD_COLDCHAIN names the seafood wholesalers (Pucci, Santa Monica, Sierra Gold, Catalina/Baja), states the 35%+ food-cost reality, and specifies cold-chain integrity and spoilage-risk controls

competency_questions.question: How is roasted coffee sourced, and when does an in-house house roast beat buying wholesale roasted?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COFFEE_ROASTER compares a regional roaster-wholesaler against a house roast using the deep-dive's green ($4-7/lb) vs wholesale-roasted ($8-14/lb) margin lever and the volume that justifies roasting

competency_questions.question: How are equipment, smallwares, and the disposables/packaging stream sourced and replenished?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EQUIPMENT_SMALLWARES covers the format-defining capital anchor (espresso machine, kebab charbroiler, bakery ovens, batch freezer, draft system), smallwares replacement, and the paper/chem/disposables broadline stream

competency_questions.question: How are waste, grease, and recycling streams set up, and why are they a compliance gate, not an afterthought?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WASTE_GREASE specifies grease-trap/used-cooking-oil hauling, organics/recycling compliance, and the truck commissary's water/waste servicing as a permit-linked requirement

competency_questions.question: What permit, commissary, and license footprint gates a supply setup before the first order is placed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERMIT_COMMISSARY cites the public fee facts (county food-facility permit, mobile $69-$548/yr, city $900 mobile permit, $114 license, ABC Type 41/47 fees) and names the mandatory commissary for mobile

competency_questions.question: How is input cost modeled honestly without asserting any business's revenue, and how is a benchmark estimate labeled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_BENCHMARK_HONESTY derives input spend as a labeled estimate (published food-cost % x an observable size signal x format band) tagged estimate-not-actual with confidence and a CDTFA/invoice confirmation path

competency_questions.question: How does the operator harden the sourcing system against price swings, single-supplier failure, and the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation, and on what cadence is it reviewed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESILIENCE_BACKUP names backup suppliers per critical input and a substitution rule; SOURCING_REVIEW_LOOP sets a price/availability review cadence and the triggers (price spike, supplier loss, consolidation) that re-run the plan

glossary.definition: A full-range foodservice distributor (e.g., Sysco Central California in Modesto ~15 mi from Turlock, or US Foods) that delivers meat, produce, frozen, dry goods, paper, chemicals, and smallwares on credit terms with order minimums; the one-stop backbone most Turlock operators anchor on.

A membership warehouse (e.g., Restaurant Depot) where the operator drives in, pays at the register, and self-transports; lower unit cost and no delivery minimum, but no credit, no delivery, and labor/time cost to fetch — ideal for trucks and small/variable lots.

Corn dough (and the nixtamalized corn behind it) that is the base of tortillas, sopes, and tamales; sourced as commodity masa flour, fresh masa from a local tortilleria, or heirloom masa (e.g., Masienda) at a premium for differentiated Mexican formats.

A Mexican butcher shop that supplies marinated and specialty cuts (carne asada, al pastor, carnitas, lengua, tripa); a local-supply node that lets taquerias and trucks buy fresher, cheaper center-of-plate than a broadline alone, often the truck's binding cost center.

The unbroken refrigeration path from supplier through transport to storage to service; for raw seafood (mariscos) it is the highest food-safety class and the main spoilage and liability risk, governing how often and how locally fish must be bought.

A permitted permanent food facility a mobile vendor must operate in conjunction with for overnight parking, potable-water fill, wastewater/grease disposal, and prep; the Stanislaus County mobile rule makes it a non-optional supply-and-compliance node for any truck.

Roasting green coffee on-site instead of buying wholesale roasted; the deep-dive prices green at $4-7/lb vs $8-14/lb wholesale roasted, making it a real margin lever once volume and a roaster justify the capital and labor.

The genuine cost-and-freshness edge Turlock operators get from sitting in California's top dairy county group and a major produce/almond/poultry/egg belt: short freight and direct-from-grower/carniceria/dairy options coastal metros cannot match, strongest for creamery, pizzeria cheese, cafe dairy, and panaderia eggs.

An input-spend figure built as published food-cost percentage times an observable size signal (seats, sqft, daily covers, format) times the format revenue band, explicitly tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a confirmation path — never a claim of a named business's actual spend or revenue.

Sysco's announced 2026 acquisition of Jetro/Restaurant Depot, a supply-chain watch item the deep-dive flags because it could consolidate Central Valley cash-and-carry pricing that many small Turlock operators rely on, raising single-channel dependence risk.

nodes.definition: Pin down, for the operator's specific Turlock format, which input is the dominant cost center the deep-dive marks in bold and how the remaining inputs rank by spend and risk: marinated meats and tortillas for taqueria/truck, fresh shrimp/fish/oysters for mariscos, mozzarella for pizzeria, hand-shaping labor plus flour/lard for panaderia, roasted coffee plus milk for cafe, premium center-of-plate for fine dining, halal lamb/chicken plus rice and spices for Assyrian, dairy cream for ice cream. This profile is the raw input that bounds every channel and supplier choice downstream.

included: input ranking by cost share and risk
the inputs the plan must protect first

pros.claim: Naming the one dominant cost center focuses sourcing effort where margin is actually won or lost
pros.example: a pizzeria that recognizes mozzarella as its volatile center prioritizes a dairy-contract relationship over chasing cheaper canned tomatoes

cons.claim: Over-fixating on the single biggest input can starve attention from a smaller input with higher spoilage or stockout risk
cons.example: a mariscos kitchen optimizing fish price while letting lime and cilantro stockouts halt the aguachile line

failure_modes: importing another format's cost profile so the wrong input is protected
treating labor-heavy formats like panaderia as ingredient-cost problems when hand-shaping labor dominates
acceptance_tests: the profile names the format's dominant cost center exactly as the deep-dive marks it and ranks at least three more inputs by cost share and risk
revisit_triggers: the operator changes or adds a format or menu line
a previously minor input becomes the binding cost or risk

base.update_signal: the format, menu, or dominant input cost center changes

nodes.definition: Enumerate the realistic supplier universe verified to serve Turlock/Modesto/Central Valley and segment it by channel: broadline (Sysco Central California in Modesto, US Foods), cash-and-carry (Restaurant Depot), local ag (Central Valley dairies, produce houses, carnicerias such as La Rancherita and La Morenita), tortilla/masa houses, ethnic importers, seafood wholesalers, regional roasters, equipment/smallwares dealers, and waste/grease haulers. Each node is tagged verified-to-serve-this-geography versus representative inference, because supplier-to-named-business links are inference unless the deep-dive cites them.

pros.claim: A pre-mapped, geography-verified supplier list stops the operator from cold-calling vendors who do not deliver to Turlock
pros.example: knowing Sysco's Modesto house is ~15 miles out avoids chasing a Bay Area distributor with a minimum that excludes the county

cons.claim: A fixed universe can ossify and miss a new local entrant or a vendor that recently extended delivery into the county
cons.example: overlooking a newly opened regional produce house because it postdates the deep-dive snapshot

failure_modes: treating an inferred supplier link as a confirmed contract
omitting the local-grocer-as-supplier nodes that ethnic formats depend on
acceptance_tests: the universe lists at least eight channel segments with at least one named, geography-verified provider each, and tags every named-business link as verified or inference
revisit_triggers: a supplier opens, closes, merges, or changes its Turlock delivery reach
the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation alters the cash-and-carry landscape

base.update_signal: the verified supplier set or its Turlock delivery reach changes

nodes.definition: Establish the permit, license, and commissary footprint that gates any supply setup before the first order: the Stanislaus County food-facility health permit required for every fixed facility (plan check plus annual permit), the mobile food-facility county permit at $69-$548/yr by risk category, the City of Turlock mobile-vendor permit at $900 and business license at $114, the mandatory commissary a mobile vendor must operate in conjunction with, and the ABC Type 41 (app ~$905) versus Type 47 (app $6,275-$16,560 plus a secondary-market license that can exceed $100k-$200k) fee facts. These are cited public fees, and the commissary is a non-optional supply node for trucks.

included: county and city food and mobile permit fees

pros.claim: Pricing the permit and commissary gate up front prevents a truck or bar concept from ordering inventory it cannot yet legally serve
pros.example: a would-be truck operator budgets the $900 city permit, $69-$548 county fee, $114 license, and a commissary contract before buying a single case of meat

cons.claim: Treating every fee as fixed can over-state the entry gate for a low-risk fixed cafe that needs only the basic county food permit
cons.example: a beverage-only coffee shop assuming the six-figure Type 47 wall applies when it needs no liquor license at all

failure_modes: a truck arranging supply with no commissary so it cannot legally service water/waste
under-budgeting the Type 47 secondary-market license for a bar-forward concept
acceptance_tests: the relevant permit, license, and (for mobile) commissary requirements are listed with their cited public fee figures before any supplier order is placed
revisit_triggers: a county or city fee schedule or the ABC fee table changes
the operator adds a mobile unit or an alcohol program

base.update_signal: a permit, license, commissary, or ABC fee requirement changes

nodes.definition: Characterize the genuine Central Valley input advantage the deep-dive documents: Turlock sits in California's #1 dairy county group and a major produce, almond, poultry, and egg belt, giving short freight, direct-from-grower, carniceria, and dairy options plus a dense Mexican/Assyrian/Portuguese grocery ecosystem that doubles as specialty supply. This structural edge on dairy, eggs, produce, and meat is what lets creameries, pizzerias (cheese), cafes (milk), panaderias (eggs), and chef-forward kitchens undercut coastal-metro input costs and run fresher.

pros.claim: Quantifying the Valley advantage tells the operator which inputs are cheaper to buy local than through a national broadline
pros.example: an in-house creamery sourcing cream from a local dairy at a freight and freshness edge a coastal shop cannot match

cons.claim: The advantage is real for commodity ag but does not extend to specialty ethnic or marine inputs that must still be imported
cons.example: assuming the dairy edge helps with basmati rice or Baja shrimp, which it does not

failure_modes: over-claiming the advantage for inputs the Valley does not produce
ignoring that direct-from-grower requires volume and handling the operator may lack
acceptance_tests: the analysis names the specific Valley-produced inputs that carry a cost/freshness edge and the formats that capture it, distinguishing them from imported inputs that do not
revisit_triggers: a local ag price shock (drought, feed, fuel) erodes the advantage
a direct-grower relationship opens or closes

base.update_signal: local ag pricing or direct-grower access materially shifts

nodes.definition: Decide the percentage split of purchasing spend across broadline, cash-and-carry, and local/direct channels for the specific format and volume, rather than defaulting to a single source. The mix is driven by order volume (broadline minimums favor higher-volume sit-downs), format (trucks and panaderias lean cash-and-carry and local for variable small lots), the cost-versus-resilience tradeoff (one-stop convenience versus multi-source price leverage and backup), and the Valley advantage that pulls dairy/produce/meat toward local. The output is a reasoned target split with the rationale for each slice.

included: target percentage split across the three channel types
excluded: the detailed terms of any one channel

pros.claim: An explicit multi-channel split captures the unit-cost win of cash-and-carry and the freshness win of local without losing broadline's one-stop backbone
pros.example: a taqueria anchoring dry/paper on Sysco, buying produce and small meat lots from a carniceria, and topping up at Restaurant Depot on weekends

cons.claim: Spreading spend across too many channels raises ordering, receiving, and reconciliation labor and can drop below each vendor's best-price tier
cons.example: a tiny cafe splitting milk across three sources and qualifying for no volume discount anywhere

failure_modes: single-sourcing everything on broadline for convenience and overpaying on every commodity input
fragmenting spend so finely that no channel gives a volume break
acceptance_tests: a target spend split across broadline, cash-and-carry, and local/direct is stated with a volume- and format-grounded rationale for each slice
revisit_triggers: order volume crosses a broadline minimum or a cash-and-carry break point
a channel's pricing or the Valley advantage shifts the optimal mix

base.update_signal: volume, format, or channel pricing changes the optimal split

nodes.definition: Set up the broadline distributor relationship that anchors most Turlock operators: Sysco Central California in Modesto (~15 miles, carrying meat, produce, frozen, dry, paper, chem, and smallwares) or US Foods as the one-stop backbone delivering on credit terms with order minimums. The node covers negotiating the account, understanding minimums and delivery windows, using the rep for price tracking, and recognizing that broadline convenience beats cash-and-carry once volume clears the minimum and delivery labor is valued.

included: account setup, minimums, delivery, credit terms
excluded: specialty inputs broadline does not carry

pros.claim: A single delivered broadline account saves the labor of self-fetching and gives credit terms that ease cash flow for a higher-volume kitchen
pros.example: a sit-down Mexican restaurant taking weekly Sysco delivery on terms instead of sending staff to Modesto to haul cases

cons.claim: Broadline unit prices run above cash-and-carry, and order minimums can force over-ordering for a small operator
cons.example: a low-volume cafe padding an order to hit a delivery minimum and carrying perishables it cannot sell

failure_modes: accepting list pricing without using the rep or a buying group for leverage
missing that the format's volume sits below the broadline-economic threshold
acceptance_tests: the broadline account terms (minimum, delivery window, credit) are documented and the volume threshold above which broadline beats cash-and-carry is stated for this format
revisit_triggers: the distributor changes minimums, delivery reach, or pricing
the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation alters broadline leverage

base.update_signal: broadline terms, pricing, or delivery reach change

nodes.definition: Use cash-and-carry (Restaurant Depot membership) where lower unit cost, no delivery minimum, and the freedom to buy exactly the variable small lots a truck or small kitchen needs outweigh the labor and time of self-transport and pay-now-no-credit terms. This is the natural fit for taco trucks (which already buy smaller lots), panaderias topping up, and any operator filling gaps or chasing a better commodity price than the broadline rep will match.

included: fit for trucks and small/variable lots

pros.claim: Cash-and-carry lets a truck or small kitchen buy exactly what it needs at a lower unit cost than a delivered broadline minimum allows
pros.example: a taco truck buying two cases at Restaurant Depot for a weekend event instead of meeting a broadline delivery minimum

cons.claim: The model spends staff time and vehicle cost on the run and offers no credit, straining cash flow when receipts are tight
cons.example: an owner losing a prep morning to a Modesto warehouse round-trip during a labor crunch

failure_modes: treating cash-and-carry as a full substitute for delivery at high volume
over-relying on a single warehouse exposed to the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation
acceptance_tests: the cash-and-carry role is defined with the lot sizes and inputs it covers and the labor/credit tradeoff against delivered broadline is stated
revisit_triggers: the warehouse changes membership terms or pricing
the consolidation shifts cash-and-carry pricing for small operators

base.update_signal: cash-and-carry terms, pricing, or consolidation status change

nodes.definition: Set up direct or near-direct local sourcing of the inputs the Central Valley produces best: dairy and cream from local dairies, produce from Valley produce houses, eggs from local farms, and meat from carnicerias (La Rancherita, La Morenita) that supplement the broadline. This is how a Turlock operator converts the Valley advantage into actual cost and freshness, documented for the format that markets it (La Mo's sources fresh ingredients from local farms; chef-forward fine dining leans on local farms and ranches). It trades a little more vendor management for fresher, cheaper center inputs.

included: converting the Valley advantage to real spend

pros.claim: Direct local sourcing delivers fresher product at a freight advantage and a marketing story chains cannot copy
pros.example: La Mo's documented fresh-from-local-farms sourcing as both a cost edge and a customer-facing differentiator

cons.claim: Direct relationships add ordering, quality-control, and reliability overhead and can leave gaps a broadline would have filled
cons.example: a small farm's seasonal produce gap forcing a last-minute broadline order at a worse price

failure_modes: assuming a direct-grower link is documented when it is only representative inference
outgrowing a small supplier's capacity without a backup
acceptance_tests: at least two locally produced inputs are routed to a named or representative local supplier with the freshness/cost rationale and a noted reliability backup
revisit_triggers: a local supplier gains or loses capacity or quality
the Valley advantage shifts the local-vs-broadline economics

base.update_signal: a local supplier's capacity, quality, or pricing changes

nodes.definition: Set up the masa/tortilla and carniceria supply that anchors taqueria, taco-truck, and sit-down Mexican formats. Tortillas and chips come from a Valley tortilla/masa house (The Tortilla Plug, Romero's Food Products, Mi Rancho), heirloom masa from Masienda for a differentiated menu, or fresh from a local tortilleria (Tortilleria Tres Hermanos); marinated meats (asada, al pastor, carnitas, lengua, tripa) — the format's bold cost center — come from local carnicerias plus broadline, with trucks buying smaller lots via cash-and-carry. The node matches tortilla type and lot size to volume and concept.

included: tortilla/masa house vs local tortilleria vs heirloom masa
lot-size matching to truck vs restaurant

pros.claim: Matching tortilla source and meat lot size to the concept controls the taqueria's dominant meat cost while protecting authenticity
pros.example: a 15-year cash-only taco truck buying marinated meats in small carniceria lots that match its daily volume with no waste

cons.claim: Heirloom masa and specialty marinades cost more and can over-engineer a value-priced, high-volume counter concept
cons.example: a value taqueria paying a Masienda premium its price point cannot recover

failure_modes: sourcing tortillas at a lot size that stales before use
single-sourcing marinated meat with no carniceria backup during a price spike
acceptance_tests: the tortilla/masa source and the marinated-meat (carniceria/broadline) source are named with lot sizes matched to the format's volume
revisit_triggers: a tortilla house or carniceria changes price, availability, or quality
the concept shifts between value-volume and premium-authentic

base.update_signal: tortilla/masa or carniceria sourcing terms change

nodes.definition: Route the specialty ethnic inputs a broadline does not carry to the right importer and local-grocer supply, the backbone of Turlock's heritage formats. This node is the umbrella that segments Mexican specialty (dried chiles, piloncillo, Clamato), Assyrian/Middle-Eastern (Sadaf/Soofer, Zarrin, Karabetian, Macar plus local grocers Nineveh Imports, International Bazar, Neesan Market), Portuguese/Azorean specialty, and Bay Area Asian importers for the pan-Asian SKU breadth. It also flags that local ethnic markets double as supply (Ishtar's own market is part supplier) and that multi-cuisine concepts carry the most vendors.

excluded: the Assyrian and Portuguese deep-dive specifics handled in their own nodes

pros.claim: Mapping each community's importer chain unlocks authentic inputs the broadline cannot supply and that anchor the format's identity
pros.example: an Assyrian grill sourcing spices and lavash through Karabetian and a local Assyrian grocer rather than a generic distributor

cons.claim: Specialty importers carry higher freight, higher minimums, and longer lead times than a local broadline delivery
cons.example: a single-SKU spice order from a San Jose importer arriving days later than a Modesto broadline drop

failure_modes: running a multi-cuisine line through one importer that cannot cover every cuisine, raising SKU waste
missing that a local heritage grocer is a faster, cheaper supply node than a distant importer
acceptance_tests: each ethnic input family on the menu is routed to a named importer or local-grocer supply node, and multi-cuisine SKU/vendor breadth is flagged where it applies
revisit_triggers: an importer changes minimums, lead time, or availability
the menu adds or drops a cuisine line

base.update_signal: an importer or local-grocer supply node changes terms or availability

nodes.definition: Set up the Assyrian/Middle-Eastern supply chain that serves Turlock's defining ~20,000-strong Assyrian community and its kebab houses, grills, and markets: halal lamb and chicken as the center-of-plate cost, plus basmati rice, bulgur, spices, tahini, olives, and lavash/flatbread. Inputs route through Mediterranean/Assyrian importers (Sadaf/Soofer, Zarrin, Karabetian since 1987, Macar) and local halal markets (Turlock Halal Market) and Assyrian grocers, with the documented case that a market-and-grill like Ishtar acts as part of its own supply.

included: local halal and Assyrian grocer supply
excluded: the grill equipment (handled in equipment node)

pros.claim: A dedicated Assyrian supply chain secures halal proteins and authentic staples that a generic broadline cannot certify or stock
pros.example: a kebab house contracting halal lamb through a halal market while buying spices and lavash via Karabetian

cons.claim: Halal-certified protein and imported staples carry premiums and supply-continuity risk a commodity meat order does not
cons.example: a halal lamb shortage forcing a substitution that the community clientele notices

failure_modes: assuming generic meat passes for a halal-expecting clientele
single-sourcing lavash or spices with no second importer
acceptance_tests: halal protein and at least three Assyrian staple inputs are each routed to a named importer or local halal/Assyrian grocer with a noted backup
revisit_triggers: a halal supplier or Mediterranean importer changes availability or certification
the community-facing menu changes its staple mix

base.update_signal: halal protein or Assyrian-staple supply changes

nodes.definition: Set up the Portuguese/Azorean specialty supply that serves Turlock's ~7.3% Azorean-ancestry community and its bakeries: specific flours, sugar, eggs, butter/lard, and yeast plus Portuguese specialty ingredients with linguica/chourico adjacency, much of it festa-concentrated. Inputs route through broadline and bakery distributors for the bulk staples, Portuguese/specialty importers serving the Azorean community for the heritage items, and local eggs/dairy from Azorean-rooted dairies — a format the deep-dive marks as under-served and the most seasonal in the set, so the supply plan must flex for festa-season bulk peaks.

pros.claim: A festa-aware Portuguese supply plan lets a bakery scale bulk staples for event peaks without carrying that cost year-round
pros.example: a bakery pre-booking flour, sugar, and egg volume against the festa-season order book and trimming back after

cons.claim: Festa concentration creates a cash-flow and spoilage risk that an annual sourcing plan averages away
cons.example: over-ordering perishable inputs for a festa that draws fewer orders than the prior year

failure_modes: treating seasonal festa demand as steady-state and over-committing supply
missing the local Azorean-dairy egg/dairy edge and over-paying a distributor
acceptance_tests: Portuguese specialty and bulk-staple inputs are routed to named or representative suppliers with an explicit festa-season bulk-flex plan
revisit_triggers: the festa-season order book changes materially
a Portuguese importer or local dairy changes terms

base.update_signal: festa demand or Portuguese-specialty supply changes

nodes.definition: Set up fresh-seafood sourcing for the mariscos format — the highest food-cost (often 35%+) and highest-risk case in the set. Shrimp, fish, oysters, and octopus route through seafood wholesalers (Pucci Foods since 1918, Santa Monica Seafood, Sierra Gold Seafood, Catalina Offshore whose Baja species fit Sinaloa-style menus) plus broadline frozen and Mexican importers for sauces and Clamato, with local produce for the cold line. Because raw seafood is the most price-volatile and most cold-chain-dependent input, sourcing cadence is short and local, and price exposure is actively managed.

included: short, local sourcing cadence for the cost-and-risk center

pros.claim: Matching seafood wholesalers to the menu style secures the right species at the freshness the highest-risk format demands
pros.example: a Sinaloa-style raw bar sourcing Baja species through Catalina rather than a generic frozen broadline pack

cons.claim: Fresh seafood's price volatility and 35%+ food cost expose the format to margin swings no other format faces
cons.example: a shrimp price spike compressing margin on every aguachile and coctel that week

failure_modes: over-ordering perishable seafood that spoils before sale
single-sourcing one wholesaler with no backup during a shortage
acceptance_tests: seafood inputs are routed to at least two named wholesalers matched to the menu style, with a short sourcing cadence and an acknowledgment of the 35%+ food-cost and price-volatility reality
revisit_triggers: a seafood price spike or shortage
a wholesaler changes species availability or delivery reach

base.update_signal: seafood price, species availability, or wholesaler reach changes

nodes.definition: Source roasted coffee for the cafe/coffeehouse format and decide between a regional roaster-wholesaler (Chatz Roasting in Ceres) and an in-house house roast. The deep-dive prices green coffee at $4-7/lb against $8-14/lb wholesale roasted, making a house roast a real margin lever (one Turlock cafe per catalog may use a house roast) once volume, a roaster, and the labor justify the capital; below that volume, a regional roaster-wholesaler with consistent supply and no roasting overhead wins. The node also covers milk/alt-milk (local dairy edge), syrups, and cups/lids via broadline or cash-and-carry.

included: regional roaster vs house roast decision

pros.claim: A house roast captures the green-vs-roasted spread and a differentiation story once volume supports it
pros.example: a higher-volume cafe roasting green at $4-7/lb instead of buying roasted at $8-14/lb and branding the house roast

cons.claim: House roasting adds capital, labor, consistency risk, and waste that a low-volume shop cannot absorb
cons.example: a student-traffic cafe under the volume threshold producing stale or uneven roast batches

failure_modes: roasting in-house below the volume that justifies the capital and labor
single-sourcing one roaster-wholesaler with no backup for a core SKU
acceptance_tests: the roasted-coffee decision states the regional-roaster option and the house-roast break-even using the green-vs-roasted spread, with milk/syrup/cup sourcing routed
revisit_triggers: coffee volume crosses the house-roast break-even
the roaster-wholesaler or green-coffee price changes

base.update_signal: coffee volume, green price, or roaster terms change

nodes.definition: Source the format-defining capital equipment, the replaceable smallwares, and the recurring disposables stream. The capital anchor differs by format — espresso machine and grinders for cafes, charbroiler/kebab grill for Assyrian, revolving/rack ovens, mixers, sheeters, and proofers for bakeries, batch freezer/pasteurizer/hardening freezer for in-house ice cream, a draft system for a tap house, a heavy cold line for mariscos — and is bought through equipment dealers or used-equipment channels. Smallwares (pans, utensils, wares) and the paper/chem/disposables/packaging stream flow through the broadline (Sysco carries them) or cash-and-carry on an ongoing replenishment basis.

pros.claim: Identifying the format's capital anchor and a smallwares/disposables replenishment channel prevents a stockout of a wear item from halting service
pros.example: a cafe pairing a reliable espresso-machine service contract with a broadline cup/lid standing order

cons.claim: Over-buying new capital equipment when a used unit would serve ties up cash the thin-margin format needs for inventory
cons.example: a startup bakery buying a new rack oven when a refurbished one met its volume

failure_modes: no smallwares/disposables replenishment plan so a wear item stockout stops the line
buying capital equipment mismatched to the format's volume
acceptance_tests: the format's capital anchor is identified with a sourcing channel and a recurring smallwares/disposables replenishment source is named
revisit_triggers: a capital item fails or the format's volume outgrows it
a disposables or smallwares supplier changes pricing

base.update_signal: a capital anchor, smallwares, or disposables source changes

nodes.definition: Set up the outbound waste streams that are a compliance gate, not an afterthought: used-cooking-oil and grease-trap servicing by a licensed grease/UCO hauler, organics and recycling compliance under California mandates, and — for any mobile unit — the commissary's potable-water fill and wastewater/grease disposal that the Stanislaus County mobile rule requires. A fixed kitchen schedules grease-trap pumping and UCO pickup; a truck cannot legally operate without a commissary servicing these streams.

pros.claim: Treating waste/grease as a scheduled, permitted service avoids the health and compliance violations that can shut a facility
pros.example: a fryer-heavy kitchen on a regular grease-trap pumping and UCO-pickup schedule that passes inspection

cons.claim: Over-frequent hauling on a low-volume kitchen wastes money on a stream that could be serviced less often
cons.example: a low-fry cafe paying for weekly grease service it does not generate

failure_modes: a truck operating with no commissary water/waste servicing and failing inspection
an unscheduled grease trap overflowing into a health violation
acceptance_tests: grease/UCO hauling and organics/recycling are scheduled with a named service, and any mobile unit has commissary water/waste servicing in place
revisit_triggers: a waste/recycling mandate or hauler contract changes
fry/waste volume changes the servicing cadence

base.update_signal: a waste/grease mandate or hauler arrangement changes

nodes.definition: Protect cold-chain integrity and food-safety compliance across receiving, storage, and prep — the handling discipline that makes the seafood, dairy, and meat sourcing decisions safe. It covers receiving-temperature checks, unbroken refrigeration from delivery to service, HACCP-style handling for the highest-risk inputs (raw seafood is the top food-safety class), and the county food-program inspection standards. Strong receiving discipline both prevents spoilage loss on the most expensive inputs and is the precondition for the short, fresh sourcing cadence mariscos and dairy demand.

pros.claim: Disciplined cold-chain receiving converts the local fresh-sourcing advantage into actual yield by cutting spoilage on the costliest inputs
pros.example: temperature-checking every seafood delivery and rejecting an out-of-spec load before it spoils a day's coctel sales

cons.claim: Strict receiving and cold-chain controls add labor and can slow intake during a rush
cons.example: a busy delivery morning where temp-logging every case delays the prep start

failure_modes: a broken cold chain spoiling high-cost seafood or dairy before service
skipping receiving checks and accepting an out-of-spec load
acceptance_tests: receiving-temperature checks and unbroken-refrigeration handling are specified for the high-risk inputs, consistent with county food-program standards
revisit_triggers: a food-safety incident or failed inspection
a new high-risk input is added to the menu

base.update_signal: a food-safety standard, incident, or high-risk input changes

nodes.definition: Manage the input price swings that move a thin-margin operator's net: mozzarella for pizzeria (partly offset by the Valley dairy advantage), shrimp and fish for mariscos, butter and eggs for bakeries, and broadline commodity drift, plus the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation that could shift cash-and-carry pricing many small operators rely on. The node tracks the format's most volatile inputs, watches the consolidation as a structural risk, and feeds the substitution and review decisions that keep a price spike from quietly erasing the 3-12% net the deep-dive documents.

pros.claim: Watching the few most volatile inputs lets an operator hedge or substitute before a spike eats the thin net margin
pros.example: a pizzeria leaning on the Valley dairy advantage and a dairy contract to blunt a mozzarella price spike

cons.claim: Reacting to every short-term price wiggle churns suppliers and menus more than the margin gain justifies
cons.example: re-pricing the menu on a transient shrimp blip that reverses the next week

failure_modes: ignoring the consolidation risk until cash-and-carry pricing jumps
treating a transient spike as permanent and over-correcting
acceptance_tests: the format's two or three most volatile inputs are named with a watch and a substitution/hedge trigger, and the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation is logged as a structural risk
revisit_triggers: a tracked input price spikes or the consolidation advances
a hedge or substitution rule fires

base.update_signal: a volatile input price or the consolidation status changes

nodes.definition: Harden the sourcing system against single-supplier failure by naming a backup source and a substitution rule for each critical input, so a stockout, a price spike, or a lost vendor does not halt service. The multi-channel mix already gives partial redundancy; this node makes it explicit: a second carniceria behind the primary, a second seafood wholesaler, a backup tortilla house, a fallback from local-direct to broadline when a small grower's capacity gaps, and a documented response to the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation concentrating cash-and-carry. Resilience is bought with a little redundancy cost against the larger cost of a service-stopping outage.

included: a backup source per critical input
the substitution rule and fallback path

pros.claim: A named backup per critical input turns a supplier outage from a service-stopping crisis into a routine substitution
pros.example: a taqueria switching to its second carniceria the day the primary runs short of asada with no menu gap

cons.claim: Maintaining backups across every input adds qualification effort and can split volume below each vendor's best price
cons.example: qualifying a second produce house used so rarely it never earns a volume break

failure_modes: single-sourcing the dominant cost center with no backup
naming a backup never actually qualified, so it fails when called on
acceptance_tests: each critical input has a named backup source and a substitution rule, with an explicit response to the cash-and-carry consolidation risk
revisit_triggers: a primary supplier is lost or a backup becomes unavailable
the consolidation concentrates a previously redundant channel

base.update_signal: a primary or backup supplier's availability changes

nodes.definition: Model input spend honestly as a labeled benchmark estimate and never as a named business's actual figure. Method: take the published food-cost percentage for the format (QSR 28-32%, casual 30-34%, fine dining 32-35%, mariscos 35%+) times an observable size signal (seats, sqft, daily covers, format) times the format's revenue band ($300k-$700k typical independent; full-service to ~$1.2M; the ~$0.9M-$1.25M sector figure is a pool mean, not a typical business), tag the result estimate-not-actual with a confidence level, and state the confirmation path (operator invoices or CDTFA/Turlock sales-tax receipts). This keeps every dollar figure a disciplined planning estimate.

included: food-cost % x size signal x format band method

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark method gives a usable input-spend estimate without ever asserting a private business's actual figures
pros.example: estimating a cafe's monthly coffee spend as COGS% x daily transactions x band, tagged medium-confidence with an invoice confirmation path

cons.claim: Benchmark estimates carry real uncertainty and can mislead if their estimate-not-actual label is dropped downstream
cons.example: a planning estimate quoted later as if it were a measured cost

failure_modes: stating a per-business dollar figure as fact instead of a labeled estimate
using the pool-mean sector average as if it were a typical business
acceptance_tests: every input-spend figure is derived as benchmark % x size signal x format band, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level and a named confirmation path
revisit_triggers: a published cost-structure benchmark updates
actual invoice or CDTFA data becomes available to replace an estimate

base.update_signal: a cost benchmark updates or actual cost data becomes available

nodes.definition: Assemble the consolidated sourcing plan that turns the scattered channel and supplier decisions into one operating system: the channel-mix split, the named primary and backup supplier per input family, the order cadence and lot sizes per channel, the cold-chain and waste compliance hooks, the labeled cost estimate per major input, and the permit/commissary preconditions cleared. It is the single artifact an operator works from to place the first orders and run weekly purchasing.

included: primary/backup per input with cadence and lot size
excluded: individual node decisions already made upstream

pros.claim: One consolidated plan converts a pile of channel decisions into an executable weekly purchasing system with no orphaned input
pros.example: a single sheet listing every input, its primary and backup, its channel, cadence, and lot size that staff order from each week

cons.claim: A fixed plan can ossify and ignore a better mid-stream sourcing opportunity if not paired with a review loop
cons.example: sticking to a broadline line item when a new local grower would beat it on price and freshness

failure_modes: a plan with an input that has no assigned supplier or backup
compliance hooks (cold chain, commissary, permits) left off the plan
acceptance_tests: the plan lists every major input family with a primary supplier, a backup, a channel, a cadence, and a lot size, plus the compliance and labeled-cost hooks
revisit_triggers: a supplier, channel, or compliance requirement in the plan changes
the review loop flags a better sourcing path

base.update_signal: a supplier, channel, cadence, or compliance element of the plan changes

nodes.definition: Define the loop that keeps the sourcing plan alive: a fixed price-and-availability review cadence (e.g., monthly broadline price-list check plus a quarterly full-mix review) and the material-change triggers — a tracked input price spike, a lost or merged supplier, the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation landing, a menu or format change, a failed inspection — that send the operator back through FORMAT_COST_PROFILE and CHANNEL_MIX to re-plan. Without this loop the sourcing plan silently drifts out of cost and resilience alignment.

included: re-entry into cost profile and channel mix

pros.claim: A scheduled review catches price drift and supplier risk before they compress the thin margin for months
pros.example: a quarterly mix review that spots a broadline line item now beaten by a local grower and reroutes it

cons.claim: Reviewing too often churns suppliers and prevents any relationship or volume break from maturing
cons.example: re-tendering every input monthly so no vendor ever grants a loyalty price

failure_modes: no cadence set so the plan is never revisited and drifts
ignoring a material-change trigger and running a now-misaligned plan
acceptance_tests: a review cadence and an explicit list of material-change triggers exist, each routing back to FORMAT_COST_PROFILE and CHANNEL_MIX
revisit_triggers: a material-change trigger fires
the cadence proves too frequent or too sparse

base.update_signal: a material-change trigger fires or the cadence is tuned

edges.why_related: the channel split is built around protecting the format's dominant cost center
the Valley advantage is read off the local-ag segment of the verified supplier universe
the local-input advantage pulls dairy/produce/meat spend toward the local slice of the mix
the commissary and permit gate constrains which channels a mobile or new operator can even use
the broadline slice of the mix sets up the distributor account and terms
the cash-and-carry slice of the mix defines what is bought at the warehouse
the local/direct slice of the mix sets up direct grower and carniceria sourcing
direct local sourcing is the mechanism that converts the Valley advantage into real spend
the taqueria meat-and-tortilla cost center defines the masa/carniceria sourcing need
tortilla and meat lot sizes are matched to the channel mix and format volume
the ethnic-importer segment of the supplier universe is the routing source for specialty inputs
which specialty inputs must be imported follows from the format's menu and cost profile
Assyrian halal and staple routing is a specialization of the ethnic-importer umbrella
Portuguese/Azorean specialty routing is a specialization of the ethnic-importer umbrella
Azorean-rooted local dairies supply the eggs and dairy the Portuguese bakery format leans on
the mariscos seafood cost-and-risk center defines the seafood sourcing setup
the seafood-wholesaler segment of the supplier universe is the routing source for fish and shrimp
the cafe roasted-coffee cost center defines the roaster-vs-house-roast decision and routes its milk/syrup/cup inputs
the format's capital anchor is determined by its production needs and cost profile
the commissary water/waste rule and facility permit gate the waste/grease stream setup
the highest-risk seafood sourcing sets the cold-chain handling discipline that protects it
fresh local dairy and produce require the receiving and cold-chain checks that prevent spoilage
which inputs are price-volatile follows from the format's cost profile
the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation risk centers on cash-and-carry pricing
the multi-channel mix is the partial redundancy the backup plan makes explicit
the tracked volatile inputs are the ones that most need a named backup and substitution rule
the most fragile seafood supply needs a second wholesaler as backup
the taqueria's dominant meat input needs a backup carniceria
the cost estimate is built per input from the format's cost profile and food-cost band
the broadline account is a core line of the consolidated plan
the local-direct sources are core lines of the consolidated plan
the labeled cost estimate per input is a required hook in the consolidated plan
the per-input backup and substitution rules are folded into the consolidated plan
the review loop watches the consolidated plan and triggers re-planning
a menu or format change sends the operator back to re-profile the cost center
a price or supplier change re-runs the channel-mix split the plan depends on
broadline delivery convenience and credit compete head-to-head with cash-and-carry unit-cost savings for the same spend
edges.resolution_rule: route delivered, credit-needing, high-volume and minimum-clearing inputs to broadline; route small, variable, and price-sensitive lots to cash-and-carry; set the split by the format's volume against the broadline minimum

edges.why_related: direct local sourcing wins on freshness and freight but loses the broadline's one-stop reliability and gap-filling
edges.resolution_rule: buy Valley-produced dairy/produce/meat local for freshness and cost, but keep the broadline as the gap-filler and reliability backstop when a small grower's capacity gaps

edges.why_related: choosing an in-house house roast adds roaster capital and labor that compete with buying roasted from a wholesaler
edges.resolution_rule: buy wholesale roasted below the house-roast volume break-even; commit roaster capital only once volume clears the green-vs-roasted spread payback and the labor is available

edges.why_related: the most volatile seafood prices causally drive the mariscos margin swings the volatility node manages

conflict_axes.name: delivery_convenience_vs_unit_cost
conflict_axes.description: Delivered broadline with credit and one-stop convenience competes against cash-and-carry's lower unit cost and self-fetch labor for the same spend.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split by volume against the broadline minimum: delivered for high-volume credit-needing inputs, warehouse for small variable lots

conflict_axes.name: local_freshness_vs_one_stop_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Direct local sourcing wins on freshness, freight, and story but adds vendor management and reliability gaps a broadline would fill.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy Valley-produced inputs local, keep broadline as the gap-filler and reliability backstop

conflict_axes.name: single_source_simplicity_vs_resilience
conflict_axes.description: Consolidating spend with one supplier simplifies ordering and earns volume breaks but concentrates outage and price risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: single-source non-critical commodities for the volume break; always keep a qualified backup for the dominant cost center

conflict_axes.name: house_roast_vs_buy_roasted
conflict_axes.description: In-house roasting captures the green-vs-roasted spread but adds capital, labor, and consistency risk a low-volume cafe cannot absorb.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy roasted until volume clears the spread payback, then roast

conflict_axes.name: freshness_cadence_vs_price_hedging
conflict_axes.description: Frequent small fresh buys protect quality on perishables but forgo the volume buys that hedge a price spike, and vice versa.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buy perishables fresh and often; hedge only stable, storable inputs against a confirmed spike

conflict_axes.name: authenticity_premium_vs_value_cost
conflict_axes.description: Heirloom masa, halal-certified protein, and imported staples raise authenticity but cost more than commodity inputs a value concept can recover.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pay the premium where the clientele and price point reward it; use commodity inputs for value-volume concepts

conflict_axes.name: spend_consolidation_vs_volume_breaks
conflict_axes.description: Spreading spend across many channels for price and resilience can drop below each vendor's best-price tier and add reconciliation labor.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: concentrate enough volume per channel to clear its discount tier before adding another channel

conflict_axes.name: compliance_cost_vs_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Strict receiving, cold-chain, and waste-servicing discipline protects safety and yield but adds labor that slows intake and throughput.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply the strictest checks to the highest-risk inputs (seafood, dairy) and streamline low-risk receiving

conflict_axes.name: festa_peak_supply_vs_steady_cashflow
conflict_axes.description: Pre-booking festa-season bulk secures supply for the peak but risks over-commitment and spoilage if the seasonal demand falls short.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: pre-book against a confirmed festa order book, not a hoped-for one, and keep a broadline top-up option

edge_cases.description: Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation lands and cash-and-carry pricing many small operators rely on jumps
edge_cases.trigger: the announced 2026 acquisition closes and warehouse pricing shifts
edge_cases.mitigation: diversify off a single cash-and-carry source, qualify a broadline or local backup for affected inputs, and re-run the channel mix

edge_cases.description: A truck arranges supply but has no commissary, so it cannot legally service water and waste
edge_cases.trigger: a mobile vendor tries to operate without a commissary contract
edge_cases.mitigation: secure a commissary in conjunction with the truck before sourcing inventory, per the Stanislaus County mobile rule

edge_cases.description: A broken cold chain spoils a high-cost seafood load before service
edge_cases.trigger: a refrigeration gap in transport or storage on the most price-volatile input
edge_cases.mitigation: temperature-check every delivery, reject out-of-spec loads, and keep a short local sourcing cadence

edge_cases.description: A mozzarella or shrimp price spike compresses the thin net margin overnight
edge_cases.trigger: a tracked volatile input price jumps sharply
edge_cases.mitigation: lean on the Valley dairy advantage or a dairy contract for cheese, substitute or re-price for seafood, and trigger the review loop

edge_cases.description: The dominant cost-center supplier is single-sourced and runs short mid-service
edge_cases.trigger: the only carniceria or seafood wholesaler stocks out with no backup qualified
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-qualify a second source for every dominant input and switch on the substitution rule

edge_cases.description: A small local grower's capacity or quality gaps and there is no broadline fallback
edge_cases.trigger: a direct-grower relationship cannot fill a seasonal order
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the broadline as a standing gap-filler for any local-direct input

edge_cases.description: An in-house house roast is launched below the volume that justifies its capital and labor
edge_cases.trigger: a low-volume cafe roasts green before clearing the spread payback
edge_cases.mitigation: buy wholesale roasted until volume clears the green-vs-roasted break-even, then commit roaster capital

edge_cases.description: A halal-expecting clientele is served a non-certified substitute during a protein shortage
edge_cases.trigger: a halal lamb or chicken shortage forces an uncertified swap
edge_cases.mitigation: qualify a second halal supplier in advance and never substitute uncertified protein for a halal clientele

edge_cases.description: Festa-season bulk is over-committed and perishable inputs spoil when demand falls short
edge_cases.trigger: a Portuguese bakery pre-books against a hoped-for rather than confirmed festa order book
edge_cases.mitigation: pre-book against the confirmed order book and keep a broadline top-up for upside

edge_cases.description: A multi-cuisine pan-Asian line runs through one importer that cannot cover every cuisine, raising SKU waste
edge_cases.trigger: a broad menu over-extends a single specialty vendor
edge_cases.mitigation: route each cuisine to its best importer and prune low-velocity SKUs to cut waste

edge_cases.description: A grease trap is left unscheduled and overflows into a health violation
edge_cases.trigger: a fryer-heavy kitchen with no grease-service schedule
edge_cases.mitigation: schedule grease-trap pumping and UCO pickup on a cadence matched to fry volume

edge_cases.description: A per-business dollar figure is stated as fact instead of a labeled benchmark estimate
edge_cases.trigger: an input-spend or revenue number is quoted without the estimate-not-actual label
edge_cases.mitigation: derive every dollar figure as benchmark % x size signal x band, tag it estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

workflow.action: Profile the format's dominant input cost center
workflow.description: Identify the bold cost center and rank inputs by spend and risk for this format
workflow.gate: the dominant cost center is named and at least three more inputs are ranked

workflow.action: Map the verified regional supplier universe
workflow.description: Enumerate channel-segmented suppliers verified to serve Turlock and tag inference vs verified
workflow.gate: eight+ channel segments each have a named geography-verified provider

workflow.action: Clear the permit, license, and commissary gate
workflow.description: List the cited permit/license/commissary requirements before any order
workflow.gate: the relevant fees and (for mobile) commissary are documented before sourcing

workflow.action: Quantify the Central Valley input advantage
workflow.description: Name the Valley-produced inputs with a cost/freshness edge and the formats that capture it
workflow.gate: specific local-advantaged inputs and benefiting formats are named

workflow.description: Decide the broadline/cash-and-carry/local-direct split with rationale per slice
workflow.gate: a target split across the three channels with a volume/format rationale exists

workflow.action: Set up the broadline and cash-and-carry channels
workflow.description: Document broadline terms and the cash-and-carry role and threshold
workflow.gate: broadline terms and the broadline-vs-cash-and-carry threshold are documented

workflow.description: Route masa/carniceria, ethnic, seafood, and coffee inputs to named suppliers
workflow.gate: every menu input family is routed to a named or representative supplier

workflow.action: Set cold-chain, food-safety, and waste/grease controls
workflow.description: Specify receiving checks, cold-chain handling, and waste/grease servicing
workflow.gate: receiving/cold-chain handling and waste/grease servicing are specified for the risk profile

workflow.action: Build labeled cost benchmark estimates per input
workflow.description: Derive spend as benchmark % x size signal x band, tagged estimate-not-actual
workflow.gate: every input-spend figure is labeled estimate-not-actual with confidence and a confirmation path

workflow.action: Add per-input backups and price-volatility watch
workflow.description: Name a backup and substitution rule per critical input and log the consolidation risk
workflow.gate: each critical input has a named backup and substitution rule

workflow.description: Integrate channels, suppliers, cadence, lot sizes, compliance, and cost hooks
workflow.gate: every major input has a primary, backup, channel, cadence, lot size, and compliance/cost hook

workflow.action: Set the sourcing review cadence and triggers
workflow.description: Define the price/availability review and material-change triggers back to cost profile and mix
workflow.gate: a cadence and explicit trigger list routing to FORMAT_COST_PROFILE and CHANNEL_MIX exist

dominance_rules.rule: Permit and commissary readiness dominates any sourcing order
dominance_rules.rationale: no facility can legally receive or serve inventory without its food permit, and no truck without a commissary
dominance_rules.trigger: any plan to place a first supplier order
dominance_rules.action: block sourcing until the county permit and (for mobile) commissary are in place

dominance_rules.rule: Cold-chain and food-safety integrity dominates cost optimization
dominance_rules.rationale: a broken cold chain on seafood or dairy spoils the costliest inputs and creates liability that dwarfs any unit-price saving
dominance_rules.trigger: a sourcing choice trades cold-chain rigor for a lower price
dominance_rules.action: keep the cold-chain and receiving controls and find the saving elsewhere

dominance_rules.rule: Honesty labeling dominates any input-cost figure
dominance_rules.rationale: a per-business dollar number stated as fact violates the financial-honesty charter and misleads planning
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure about a named business or its inputs
dominance_rules.action: express it only as a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and a confirmation path

dominance_rules.rule: A backup for the dominant cost center dominates volume-discount consolidation
dominance_rules.rationale: an outage on the format's main input stops service, costing more than the consolidation discount earns
dominance_rules.trigger: the dominant cost center is about to be single-sourced
dominance_rules.action: qualify a second source before consolidating the rest

dominance_rules.rule: The format cost profile dominates generic channel defaults
dominance_rules.rationale: the right channel and supplier follow from which input dominates, not from a one-size broadline default
dominance_rules.trigger: a sourcing decision made before the cost center is profiled
dominance_rules.action: profile the dominant cost center first, then choose channels around it

dominance_rules.rule: Confirmed seasonal demand dominates speculative bulk pre-booking
dominance_rules.rationale: over-committing festa or peak bulk against hoped-for demand spoils perishables and strains cash flow
dominance_rules.trigger: a pre-book against an unconfirmed seasonal order book
dominance_rules.action: book only against the confirmed order book and keep a broadline top-up for upside

dominance_rules.rule: The review loop dominates impulse supplier switches
dominance_rules.rationale: structured review prevents churning a maturing supplier relationship over a transient price wiggle
dominance_rules.action: evaluate it through the review loop, not on impulse

dominance_rules.rule: Halal/authenticity certification dominates a cheaper substitute for a heritage clientele
dominance_rules.rationale: an uncertified or inauthentic swap a heritage clientele detects costs more in trust than the input saving
dominance_rules.trigger: a shortage tempts an uncertified or off-authenticity substitution
dominance_rules.action: use a pre-qualified certified backup rather than substitute down

anti_rework_rules.rule: Clear the permit and commissary gate before placing any supplier order
anti_rework_rules.prevents: buying inventory a facility or truck cannot yet legally receive or serve

anti_rework_rules.rule: Profile the dominant cost center before choosing channels and suppliers
anti_rework_rules.prevents: building a channel mix around the wrong input and re-sourcing later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify a backup for every critical input before single-sourcing it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a service-stopping outage with no substitute ready when the primary fails

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify a supplier actually delivers to Turlock before building it into the plan
anti_rework_rules.prevents: designing a plan around a vendor whose minimums or reach exclude the county

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set cold-chain receiving checks before the first perishable delivery
anti_rework_rules.prevents: spoiling high-cost seafood or dairy on day one for lack of a receiving standard

anti_rework_rules.rule: Label every input-cost figure estimate-not-actual when first written
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a planning estimate being quoted downstream as a measured per-business fact

anti_rework_rules.rule: Match tortilla and meat lot sizes to format volume before committing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: sourcing perishable lots that stale before use or stock out under volume

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pre-book seasonal bulk only against a confirmed order book
anti_rework_rules.prevents: festa or peak over-commitment that spoils perishables and strains cash

iteration_protocol.trigger: the operator changes or adds a format or menu line
iteration_protocol.action: re-profile the dominant cost center and re-run the channel mix and routing
trigger substitution or hedging and re-run the cost estimate and resilience plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: a primary supplier is lost, merges, or stocks out
iteration_protocol.action: activate the backup, re-qualify the channel, and update the plan

iteration_protocol.trigger: the Sysco/Restaurant Depot consolidation advances or closes
iteration_protocol.action: re-assess cash-and-carry dependence and diversify affected inputs

iteration_protocol.trigger: a permit, commissary, or food-safety requirement changes or an inspection fails
iteration_protocol.action: re-clear the compliance gate and adjust receiving and waste controls

iteration_protocol.trigger: order volume crosses a broadline minimum or a house-roast break-even
iteration_protocol.action: re-optimize the channel mix and the make-vs-buy decisions it gates

iteration_protocol.trigger: the festa or other seasonal peak approaches
iteration_protocol.action: flex bulk supply against the confirmed order book and set top-up backups

priority_rationale: Foundational cost-profiling, supplier-universe mapping, and the permit/commissary gate precede channel and supplier setup because every sourcing choice depends on knowing the dominant input, the verified vendor set, and the legal preconditions; the channel and format-sourcing nodes build the operating mix; resilience, honesty, and the consolidated plan compose those into a hardened, honestly-costed system; and the review loop comes last because it watches the whole plan and routes material changes back to the foundations.
